newsitem.title: FRANCE: France Telecom rival unhappy with charges.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom rival unhappy with charges.

text.p: One of France Telecom SA's future rivals said on Wednesday it was dissatisfied with interconnection charges announced earlier in the day.

"We had asked for a 30 percent cut from France Telecom's first proposals. What we have got is a 15 percent reduction. We are therefore dissatisfied," said Thierry Mileo, Bouygues Telecom's external relations director.

However, Jean-Michel Hubert, chairman of French telecoms regulator ART, said the interconnection charges were slightly higher than British Telecom but in line and often lower than the European average.
Bouygues Telecom is allied to Italy's STET and Germany's Veba.
The interconnection charges involve the amount France Telecom can bill its rivals Cegetel and Bouygues Telecom for the use of its infrastructure.
ART said the prices were 6.09 centimes for local calls and 12.78 centimes for a so-called single tandem and 17.57 centimes for a double tandem. The tariffs come into effect on January 1, 1998.
The figures were included in a detailed document which included various types of fixed costs for leased lines and other equipment.
Rival telecoms operator Cegetel, owned by Generale des Eaux, BT and Mannesmann AG, could not be immediately reached for comment.
